title: ke-…-an
pattern: ke- + root + -an: kehujanan (caught in the rain) · kebesaran (too big) · kebersihan (cleanliness)
explanation: Around a verb or a noun, ke-…-an says something happened to you that you didn't want: kehujanan (caught in the rain, from hujan), kemalingan (burgled, from maling, a thief), ketinggalan (left behind, or missed: ketinggalan bus). Around a describing word, in everyday speech, it means too … for you: Bajunya kebesaran (the top's too big), Sepatunya kekecilan (the shoes are too small). It also makes abstract nouns, the words of signs and forms: kebersihan (cleanliness), keamanan (security), kesehatan (health), kesempatan (a chance). So Hujan means it's raining, while Saya kehujanan means I got rained on.
natural: Telling people what happened to you: Saya kehujanan, Saya kecopetan di pasar (I got pickpocketed at the market). In shops, the too form is how people say something doesn't fit: Kebesaran, ada yang lebih kecil?
stiff: The too meaning (kebesaran, kemahalan, kepedasan) belongs to speech; in writing and careful speech it's terlalu: terlalu besar. And ke-…-an is never for something you chose to do: it always happened to you.

examples.english: I got caught in the rain on the way.

gap.why: The rain happened to you, unwanted, so ke-…-an; hujan alone is the rain, or it's raining.
A house that's been broken into is kemalingan; dicuri is for the thing taken (TV-nya dicuri), and maling is the thief.

examples.indonesian: Bajunya kebesaran. Ada yang lebih kecil?
examples.english: This top's too big. Do you have a smaller one?

gap.why: Too big for you is ke-…-an; besar sekali is just very big, and terbesar the biggest.
Jaga (look after) needs a noun: kebersihan, cleanliness, from bersih.
